approach: Add a `fix: bool` to `PlanEntry` (serde-skipped when false) and change the one sort in `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:783) from `(e.rung, age)` to `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`. That sort only sees the ready items of the best effective priority (plan.rs:780-781), so the flag never beats priority or dependencies. `build_capped` and `build_improving` both call `build_with`, so `athena plan` and `athena drain` get the rule without further change. Where the flag is set: the drain's `entry_of` builds every queue entry (drain.rs:4339), and it is the one path for `queue()` (drain.rs:4527) and the re-read `plan_entry` (drain.rs:4543). A new pure `mark_fixes` in drain.rs sets `fix` from record links. (1) A work item of role steward or hestia and kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, linked to the job by an evidence job reference (the steward appends the queued job last, steward.rs:712) or by an approved decision. The linked job must be on the steward channel or be the approved job. A classifier in reading/topics.rs, `is_fix_request(role, kind, touches)`, decides, and it returns false when every touched path is under `studies/` (website and study content). (2) Hestia's root-cause requests (the keys of `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`) and its gate-review requests (an open request holding the `Gate under review:` line), listed by a new `hestia::fix_requests_of`. Titles and keys are not matched, because Hestia's own rule says requests are linked by what the records link (hestia.rs:957-958). A kind Proposal from the steward is never a fix, so its website and study content requests keep their age place. The rule is recorded as D181 and in CHANGELOG.md. The plan.rs Order doc, the drain.rs module docs and the `athena drain --help` Order text are updated so they stay true.

decisions.choice: Put the fix flag in the `build_with` sort key as the first element, `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`, applied after the best-effective-priority filter.
decisions.reason: Root cause of the starvation: the order inside a tier is rung then age (plan.rs:783), and nothing says a request that fixes Athena outranks feature work. Changing the key fixes it for every caller. The ready set is already cut to the best effective priority (plan.rs:780-781) and holds only items whose dependencies are done (plan.rs:767-775), so priority, urgent/high caps and dependencies cannot be overridden. `priority_violations` compares priority only, so it stays correct.

rejected.option: Raise fix requests to a higher priority tier in memory, as `build_improving` does for repeated causes.
rejected.why: It would beat person-set high and urgent work, which the owner did not ask for and the out-of-scope list forbids, and it would consume the capped urgent and high slots.

rejected.option: Re-prioritise individual items or lean on the existing guaranteed turn (IMPROVEMENT_GAP = 2, plan.rs:466).
rejected.why: The turn only moves one request in every three and treats every steward-channel request alike, website and study content included. That is how 52 requests still starved. The brief asks for the sort key to change.

decisions.choice: Classify by typed records: `is_fix_request(role, kind, touches)` for steward work items, and `hestia::fix_requests_of` for Hestia's root-cause and gate-review requests. No title or key matching.
decisions.reason: hestia.rs:957-958 says requests are found by what the records link, never by title, and `slowdown_request` is left out for that reason (hestia.rs:970-972). Steward keys are model-chosen free text (steward.rs:895), with no stable root-cause or gate-review key to match. Kind BlindSpot and RepeatedFailure plus the Hestia links cover the owner's list: root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot, gate-review.

rejected.option: Match 'root cause' or 'gate' in the title or key, as the accepted reading allows.
rejected.why: A person's request with a similar title would jump the queue, and a reworded steward title would drop out. Both go against the records-link rule at hestia.rs:957.

rejected.option: Treat every steward-channel request as a fix (the existing `improvement_requests` set, steward.rs:376).
rejected.why: It includes website and study content requests, which the owner says are not fixes.

decisions.choice: Website and study content means every touched path is under `studies/`, and it is used as a guard. A steward request of kind Proposal is never a fix.
decisions.reason: `OUTCOME_PATHS` (drain.rs:475-478) calls `studies/` the page sources, and `xtask/` and pages.yml the generator and the publisher. A steward fix to the generator is Athena's own code, so only `studies/` counts as content. Kind Proposal is where steward content requests land (steward.rs:723-727). The guard also covers a mislabelled blind-spot request that touches only `studies/`.

rejected.why: It would demote steward fixes to `xtask/` (the site generator), which are fixes to Athena.

decisions.choice: Compute the fix set once per queue or re-read, from `Records`, in a free function `mark_fixes(entries, linked, hestia)` that takes plain data.
decisions.reason: `entry_of` runs once per queue item (drain.rs:4527-4530), and `fix_requests_of` scans the records. Taking plain `WorkItem`s lets a unit test in athena-cli cover the website and study exclusion without building a repository.

rejected.option: Compute the flag inside `entry_of` for each job.
rejected.why: It repeats the records scan for every queued item, which matters with 50 or more steward requests.

demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. Existing tests that build `PlanEntry` with `..PlanEntry::bare(..)` (plan.rs:1167, drain.rs:4907, tests/drain.rs:355) still compile because `bare` sets `fix: false`. The drain tests `six_urgent_with_two_of_athenas_own` and `with_no_improvement_request_queued_the_order_and_the_report_are_unchanged` (tests/drain.rs:395-522) keep their orders because their entries have `fix` false.
demonstrations.fails_without: A literal `PlanEntry { .. }` without `..bare` or a changed order in an existing test would fail the build or the tests.
